title: PilotANN: Memory-Bounded GPU Acceleration for Vector Search

problem.claim: Modern deep learning applications require approximate nearest neighbor search over increasingly complex, high-dimensional datasets.

gap.claim: CPU-only solutions struggle with growing computational demands, while GPU-only solutions face memory constraints.

contributions.claim: PilotANN is a hybrid CPU-GPU system for graph-based approximate nearest neighbor search that combines CPU RAM with GPU parallel processing.
PilotANN decomposes top-k search into GPU-accelerated subgraph traversal with SVD-reduced vectors, CPU refinement, and precise search with complete vectors.
PilotANN quickly selects entry points to improve search initialization while maximizing GPU utilization.

author_reported_evidence.claim: PilotANN achieves 3.9–5.4× throughput speedup on 100-million-scale datasets.
PilotANN handles datasets up to 12× larger than the available GPU memory.

narrative_sequence.summary: Approximate nearest neighbor search is increasingly important for modern deep learning applications.
CPU-only systems face computational-demand limits, while GPU-only systems face memory limits.
PilotANN addresses the limitations with a hybrid CPU-GPU architecture.
The system uses staged search precision and fast entry selection to coordinate CPU and GPU work.
The authors report throughput gains and operation on datasets exceeding GPU memory capacity.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify baseline systems, datasets beyond scale, hardware configuration, latency, recall, or evaluation methodology.
The abstract does not describe the fast entry-selection algorithm or its overhead.
